scenarios.label: Historical spending
scenarios.summary: About what Calgary spent on pavement each year from 2011 to 2025, when the budget ran between $30M and $50M.
scenarios.consequence: Pavement kept getting worse under this level of spending. After 10 years of funding at this rate, 26% of roads will be in good condition and 52% will be in poor condition (from 38% in good condition and 26% in poor condition in 2024).

scenarios.label: 2026 budget
scenarios.summary: The 2026 pavement budget, after Council moved $24M from the Fiscal Stability Reserve to reach $64M. It targets repaving 400 lane-km of road, about 2.3% of the network, so each street waits about 43 years for new pavement.
scenarios.consequence: Roads fall apart faster than they are repaired. The backlog of roads in poor condition grows.

scenarios.label: Break even
scenarios.summary: The spending that holds pavement quality steady, with no further decline.
scenarios.consequence: Funding levels match the pavement deterioration rate in 2024. The backlog of roads in poor condition remains the same.

scenarios.label: 50% of roads in good condition
scenarios.summary: The $116M a year option in the City's pavement review.
scenarios.consequence: After 10 years of funding, 50% of roads will be in good condition (up from 38% in 2024). This only covers work that was needed as of 2024, not roads that wear out after that.

scenarios.label: 60% of roads in good condition
scenarios.summary: The highest spending option in the City's pavement review.
scenarios.consequence: After 10 years of funding, 60% of roads will be in good condition (up from 38% in 2024). This would bring Calgary to the Canadian municipal average. This only covers work that was needed as of 2024, not roads that wear out after that.

scenarios.label: Seal cracks every 10 years
scenarios.summary: Crack-seal or microsurface every road at least once every 10 years.
scenarios.consequence: This only works if pavement never slips into the fair or poor categories (below 6 out of 10). Anything below 6 needs repaving. In 2024, 62% of roads were beyond crack filling.

scenarios.label: Repave every 12-17 years
scenarios.summary: Repave every road every 12 to 17 years.
scenarios.consequence: Mill and fill. This only works if pavement never slips into the poor category (below 4 out of 10). Anything below 4 needs to be rebuilt. In 2024, 26% of roads were beyond repaving.

scenarios.label: Full replacement
scenarios.summary: Rebuild every road completely when it wears out, at $300 to $350 a square metre. Local streets last 40 years, main roads 21.
scenarios.consequence: The full cost of maintaining our network if we wait until our roads fall to poor condition (below 4 out of 10).
